title: openai-compat: enforce multipart content-type validation and file payload limits for API file inputs
author: Ava Kim
release_notes: Enforce multipart content-type validation for file uploads, apply per-file and per-request payload limits, improve OpenAI-compat error messages, and add tests and docs updates.
description: Context: Several downstream partners and internal SDKs expect OpenAI-compatible behavior for file and multipart inputs (tool/file uploads, function-calling attachments, and structured inputs). We observed inconsistent content-type handling when requests used multipart/form-data vs application/json, and a few incidents where very large file uploads bypassed intended per-file/request limits which caused memory spikes in the hosted API and Dedicated runtimes. Motivation: Make file input handling predictable and compatible with OpenAI-style expectations, surface clear errors for invalid content-types, and enforce limits early in the API layer to avoid resource exhaustion. Summary of changes: - Add strict content-type validation for file-input endpoints. Multipart endpoints now explicitly accept only multipart/form-data with proper boundary headers; application/json file payloads are rejected with descriptive 400-level errors when not allowed. - Enforce per-file and per-request payload limits configurable via config (defaults chosen to match current platform SLOs): default per-file max 50MB, default total multipart payload max 100MB. Limits are enforced in the API gateway and the upload parsing middleware. - Add OpenAI-compat validation mode for the compatibility layer: when enabled, behavior mirrors OpenAI-style error codes and messages for invalid file content-type and exceeded size limits (400/413 mapping and structured JSON error bodies). - Move early validation to the ingress layer to avoid passing large payloads downstream; introduced streaming read with size checks to avoid loading entire files into memory. - Add a set of unit and integration tests (SDK integration tests with python/ts SDKs) and end-to-end tests in the perf-canary harness that simulate oversized uploads and missing boundary headers. - Update redwood-openai-compat adapter to normalize errors and document new behavior in API docs. Commits (high-level): - 1a2b3c4: add multipart content-type validator and boundary checks - 2b3c4d5: implement streaming size-limited reader for multipart parser - 3c4d5e6: add config flags and defaults for file limits; wire to ingestion layer - 4d5e6f7: openai-compat: map validation errors to OpenAI-style error responses - 5e6f7g8: tests: unit, integration, and canary scenarios + docs update Files changed (high level): - api/gateway/middleware/content_type_validator.go: new; early rejects invalid/missing content-type for endpoints expecting files. - api/gateway/middleware/stream_size_limiter.go: new; streaming read with per-file and total limits. - adapters/openai/compat/errors.go: updated; maps internal errors to OpenAI-style error objects and codes. - sdk/python/tests/test_file_uploads.py: new tests for multipart boundary and size limit behavior. - sdk/ts/tests/file_upload.spec.ts: added. - docs/api/file-uploads.md: updated with examples and error table. - infra/config/defaults.yaml: added file limits config keys. Testing and CI: - Local unit tests added; CI initially had a flaky integration test against the canary harness (timeout) which was fixed by increasing the test timeout and adding a small backoff retry in the test harness. - Final CI run: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration, canary e2e) — badge: pass. Review thread summary (condensed into single narrative): - Reviewer Noah: asked for clearer error messages and a deterministic error code mapping for SDKs; requested small refactor to keep the validator pure (no network calls). - Author (Ava): refactored validator to be pure and added explicit mapping in adapters/openai/compat/errors.go; updated docs with exact error payload examples. - Reviewer Sofia: requested that the defaults be conservative and made configurable; asked for e2e test that reproduces the memory spike scenario. - Author: added config keys in infra/defaults and an e2e perf-canary test that simulates a large multipart stream and asserts the gateway drops connection before backend allocation. - Reviewer Marcus: requested metrics for rejected uploads (400 and 413) and a note for SRE to add an alert if reject rate > 1% over 5m. - Author: added gateway metrics (api.uploads.rejected.content_type and api.uploads.rejected.size) and a short section in the observability-pack for SRE runbooks. Security review: small note from security team to ensure KMS/HSM operations unaffected; validated that changes only run at ingress and do not touch key material. Backwards compatibility: Behavior is opt-out for existing customers (openai-compat mode disabled by default); when openai-compat is enabled customers get the stricter validation and OpenAI-style errors. This avoids breaking existing private/deployed customers unless they opt into the compatibility mode. Migration notes: - For customers enabling openai-compat, SDK teams were notified to expect 400/413 mapping for malformed/missing content-type and oversize uploads. - Docs include guidance and sample code for the SDKs to handle new errors. Performance/operational notes: - Streaming checks avoid full in-memory buffering and reduced peak memory impact during tests by ~70% in the canary scenario. - Default limits chosen after testing typical workloads: 50MB/file and 100MB request total. Configurable via infra defaults and per-namespace overrides. Merge details: - PR merged via squash on 2026-02-24 after approvals from Noah and Sofia and green CI. - Changelog entry included under API/compat changes. Follow-ups: - ENG-1890: expose per-route overrides in Redwood Console for dedicated customers (follow-up ticket created). - ENG-1891: telemetry dashboard and alert knobs for SRE. Files of interest and sample snippets included inline in the PR: - content_type_validator.go: checks Content-Type header; when missing or mismatched returns {"error":{"message":"invalid content-type for file upload","type":"invalid_request_error","param":"content_type","code":null}} with 400. - stream_size_limiter.go: reads multipart parts up to limit and returns 413 with structured error when exceeded. CI note: initial run showed a single flaky canary test; rerun fixed the flake after 1 retry. All checks green. This PR addresses reported incidents INT-523 and partially covers ENG-1722. It centralizes validation and prevents large payloads from reaching downstream services, improving reliability and OpenAI-compat behavior.
